question: Show me how to take Punctual Pros nationwide
html:
Taking Punctual Pros nationwide

Take Punctual Pros nationwide in four phases: fill in Central PA, repeat the Horvath deal across the Mid-Atlantic, build an I-81/I-95 hub, then consolidate within the One Hour / Ben Franklin / Mister Sparky system. The model is Smith + Howard, which grew from ~100 professionals in one office to ~800 across 11 locations in about 3.7 years. It made nine acquisitions, grew revenue ~4x and sold to TPG Growth (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).

Starting point

  • Estimated FY2025 revenue is ~$22M, across 25 Authority Brands territories (Punctual Pros nationwide plan).
  • The core is 248 Central-PA ZIP codes with ~1.0M housing units.
  • Horvath on the Jersey Shore is the one out-of-state add-on so far.
  • System share is ~2.3% of 1,066 outlets and $831M of reported revenue.

Four expansion phases

  • Phase 1 (months 0-12): Fill in the core plus the 195 best nearby ZIP codes (144 PA, 51 MD). Close 1-2 tuck-ins from the 61-company target screen.
  • Phase 2 (months 9-24): Repeat the Horvath deal across PA, NJ, MD, DE and southern NY. That region has 54 mapped Authority territories Punctual Pros does not own. 17 PE sponsors compete for the same founders.
  • Phase 3 (months 18-36): Build a hub in Baltimore-DC, Richmond, the Philadelphia suburbs and Pittsburgh.
  • Phase 4: Become the national consolidator inside the Authority system.
  • AI layer: A 24/7 voice dispatcher, missed-call text-back and AI estimating. ServiceTitan reports 70% booking rates for its voice dispatcher, or 90% adjusted for capacity.

Across 17 companies, the sponsors that sold for more followed a similar order (Home-services company case studies):

  • Hire an integrator early.
  • Add about one company per quarter, then speed up.
  • Put every brand on one system.
  • Build membership revenue. Service Champions reached ~150,000 members, about 83 per technician.
  • Own the technician training pipeline.
